summary.intent: Execute Phase 27 (writable-shares-poc) to implement write-enabled folder sharing in CipherBox, covering API backend, owner UI, and recipient write actions.
summary.outcome: Phase 27 completed end-to-end: 3 plans executed, 4 UAT bugs fixed (per-file IPNS records, dual-key wrapping, shared save path, owner re-wrap), 8 security issues addressed via TDD, 21 E2E tests written and passing, PR created and all review comments resolved.

repo: SDK packages (@cipherbox/sdk, sdk-core, core) must be built before the web dev server can start — they are not auto-built by Vite.
Web app falls back to window.location.origin + '/api' when VITE_API_URL is unset, which resolves to the wrong port (5173 instead of 3000).
The cipher-box-ci-debug checkout does not share .env files with cipher-box — they must be copied manually.
API client (orval-generated) must be regenerated after any DTO change; the API server must be running with updated code for the OpenAPI spec to reflect changes.
Orval generates an object union type for nullable strings (nullable: true + type: string) instead of string | null — this is a known orval limitation and affects share-response DTO.
Share keys are stored in a share_keys table with keyType enum ('file', 'folder') — extended to 'file-ipns' to store recipient-wrapped IPNS private keys separately from FilePointer.
The TEE handles IPNS key signing in hardware; clients must never send plaintext IPNS keys — only TEE-encrypted versions.
Background tasks in Claude Code are killed when the conversation context shifts; use detached processes (nohup/disown) for dev servers that need to persist.
GSD phase execution uses wave-based parallel subagents; the orchestrator stays at ~10-15% context while each executor gets a fresh 200k context.

code.finding: Shared uploads set fileMetaIpnsName: '' (empty string), making uploaded files unreadable. Fix: inline full IPNS keypair generation so files get proper per-file IPNS records.
Save handler used the owner's updateFile path for all files; shared files need an onSaveSharedFile callback prop routed through SharedFileBrowser.
handleUpdateFile did not re-wrap the new file key for share recipients after owner edits, causing recipients to hold stale share_keys pointing to the old key.

withConflictRetry closures captured stale React state for currentSequenceNumber and folderChildren. Fix: add refs alongside state and sync them in all navigation and refresh functions (navigateToSubfolder, navigateUp, navigateToBreadcrumb, refreshFolderContents).
Subfolder keys were wrapped with the recipient's public key instead of the owner's, permanently locking out the owner from recipient-created subfolders.

Permission downgrade did not clean up file-ipns share_keys, allowing recipients to retain IPNS private keys post-downgrade. Fix: wrap downgrade in a transaction that deletes file-ipns keys atomically with the permission change.
createShare did not validate the permission/IPNS-key invariant: write shares require encryptedIpnsKey, read shares must not have one. Added BadRequestException guard at creation time.
MinLength(2) on ECIES ciphertext was too permissive; raised to MinLength(64). Also added @Matches(/^[0-9a-f]+$/i) and even-length hex validation to encryptedKey fields.

An overly aggressive FolderIpns ownership guard was added that blocked owners from editing recipient-uploaded files. Removed — the correct guard only prevents recipients from hijacking TEE enrollment, not from publishing to records they have write access to.
setUpgradingId was set before early returns in the upgrade handler but not cleared on those paths, leaving the UI in a permanently disabled state. Fixed with try/finally.
publishFolderIpns lookup used the calling userId instead of the sharer's userId, causing write-share recipients to fail authorization checks on publish.

workflow: TDD red-green cycle: stash fixes, write failing tests against unfixed code, pop stash, verify green. Critical for security fixes to prove the flaw existed before the fix.
Three-agent parallel code review (reuse, quality, efficiency) catches more issues than a single pass and keeps individual agent context focused.
Security review should be run after implementing crypto features; the /security:review command produces a structured report with severity levels and test case suggestions.
After removing a test that imported an exception class, always audit for unused imports — leaving them causes CI lint failures.
When NestJS unit test modules gain new service dependencies (e.g. SharesService injected into IpnsService), all affected spec files must provide mocks or CI breaks.
Detached processes (nohup + disown) are necessary for dev servers in Claude Code sessions where background tasks get killed on context shifts.
PR review comments marked 'outside of diff range' by GitHub still require resolution — check the review body directly via gh api.

friction: Background dev server tasks were killed multiple times during the session, requiring multiple restart cycles.
PostgreSQL host IP changed mid-session (192.168.133.114 → 192.168.133.12), breaking API startup; no .env existed in the debug checkout.
Web app VITE_API_URL defaulted to window.location.origin instead of localhost:3000, causing a silent 'disconnected' status with no obvious error.
SDK packages were not pre-built, blocking web dev server startup with an unresolvable module error.
Git lock file blocked commits and required manual removal.
API client regeneration required the API server to be running with updated code; regenerating against a stale server produced wrong types.
Orval generates an incorrect object union type for nullable strings; the generated model for encryptedIpnsKey was wrong but couldn't be fixed via DTO annotations alone.
NestJS watch mode did not reliably pick up DTO changes for OpenAPI spec regeneration, requiring manual server restarts.
CI caught a lint failure (unused ForbiddenException import) that local typecheck missed because ESLint and tsc have different scope.
The 'outside of diff range' GitHub review comment was not surfaced by the standard unresolved threads query, requiring direct review body inspection.
open_items: orval nullable string type generation produces 'string | ReceivedShareResponseDtoEncryptedIpnsKey' instead of 'string | null' for nullable fields — known orval limitation, deferred.
Single-share polling endpoint: current implementation fetches all received shares every 30s to detect permission changes; a targeted endpoint would be more efficient but was deferred as PoC scope.
reWrapForRecipients does not re-wrap file-ipns keys when owner edits a file — only file share_keys are updated. Recipients' IPNS write access is not refreshed on owner edits.
withConflictRetry is duplicated across 4 call sites (upload, mkdir, rename, delete); extraction into a shared helper was deferred because each site captures different locals.
The remaining `as any` cast in shares.service.spec.ts for (mockShareRepo as any).manager is intentional but could be replaced with a properly typed EntityManager mock.
E2E tests for writable shares depend on Web3Auth Core Kit init which has occasional transient timeouts — no retry logic in place.
reWrapForRecipients only handles 'file' keyType share_keys, not 'file-ipns' keys — if an owner edits a shared file, recipients' IPNS private key access is not refreshed.
